08b.name: The Great Journey
08b.note: Tartarus is a SCRIPTED fight. From H2EK's own 08b_deltacontrol_boss.hsc:  • He is ai_cannot_die, and each phase ends when his body vitality is PINNED, not when he dies (2 phases on Normal, 3 Heroic, 4 Legendary).  • The script calls unit_set_maximum_vitality on him at the start of every phase (300 Normal / 350 Heroic / 400 Legendary), so his Body Vitality and Shield Vitality cards are overwritten and do nothing here.  • The damage window opens only once his shield is chipped below 0.975 (Normal), 0.95 (Heroic) or 0.9 (Legendary), and then lasts just 2-3s (1-3s Heroic, 1-2s Legendary) before the script closes it again.  • JOHNSON'S BEAM IS REAL DAMAGE. unit_impervious is cleared on Tartarus once the fight starts and he only takes damage from the player's TEAM, which Johnson is on (ai_allegiance player human). The script tops his shield back to full immediately before each of Johnson's volleys so the break reads cleanly, then Johnson's 3-round burst chews it down. Johnson fires every 4-10s on Normal. This is why the speedrun tech is to duplicate Johnson — more beam damage per volley crosses the threshold sooner. Options has an 'Extra Johnsons (08b)' setting to try it.  • Elite reinforcements respawn on a 30-60s timer whenever 3 or fewer are alive.  So what makes this fight winnable again: extra Johnsons, your own weapon damage, and Tartarus's Gravity Hammer and AI cards — those are real tags and are not script-overridden. His vitality cards are not.

Recharge Delay.desc: How long you have to stay out of fire before your shields start refilling.
Recharge Delay.debug_desc: `Stun Time` on the player's model tag (hlmt; coll in Halo 1), set on Body and Shield together. It does not shrink the bar, it delays the refill — which makes it the most punishing single player change available.

desc_overrides.Halo 1: How long after taking a hit before your shields start coming back — `Stun Time` on the cyborg's collision tag (stock 6s). Halo 1 keeps a single value. Raising it is the single most punishing player change there is: it does not shrink the bar, it stops it refilling.
desc_overrides.Halo 2: How long after taking a hit before your shields start coming back — `Stun Time` on the player's model tag (stock 5s), set on the body and shield fields together. Covers Chief and the Arbiter alike. Raising it is the single most punishing player change there is: it does not shrink the bar, it stops it refilling.
desc_overrides.Halo 3: How long after taking a hit before your shields start coming back — `Stun Time` on the player's model tag (stock 5s), set on the body and shield fields together. Covers Chief and the Arbiter alike. Raising it is the single most punishing player change there is: it does not shrink the bar, it stops it refilling.
desc_overrides.Halo 3: ODST: How long after taking a hit before your stamina starts coming back — `Stun Time` on the ODST's model tag (stock 5s). The body field ships 0 and is held at the 1s floor. Raising it is the single most punishing player change there is: it does not shrink the bar, it stops it refilling.
desc_overrides.Halo Reach: How long after taking a hit before your shields start coming back — `Stun Time` on the Spartan's model tag (stock 7s, the longest of any game). The body field ships 999, which already means never. Raising it is the single most punishing player change there is: it does not shrink the bar, it stops it refilling.

Player Health.desc: How much damage you can take once your shields are gone.
Player Health.debug_desc: The pool itself, on the player's model tag: 75 in Halo 1, 30 in Halo 2, 45 in Halo 3, 80 in ODST. Starting Health Modifier only scales what you spawn with; this is the maximum.

Player Shield.desc: How much your shields absorb before they break.
Player Shield.debug_desc: The pool itself, on the player's model tag: 75 in Halo 1, 70 in Halo 2 and Halo 3, 80 in ODST (stamina there). Starting Shield Modifier only scales what you spawn with; this is the maximum.

Player Shield Recharge.desc: How fast your shields refill once they start coming back.
Player Shield Recharge.debug_desc: Halo 1 stores a rate per tick (the Chief's is 0.0083); Halo 2 onward store a recharge velocity (0.5). Higher is faster in both.

Death Penalty.desc: How many metagame points dying costs you — yours, and a marine's.
Death Penalty.debug_desc:
`matg globals\\globals` -> **Campaign Metagame Globals**: Player Death Point Count and Friendly Death Point Count. These are the DEATH side of the metagame and live in the map, unlike the per-kill values, which are read once from `Data\\UI\\scoredb.xml` at startup and need a restart to change.

Stock values differ by game: Halo 3 and ODST charge 25 for your own death and 50 for a marine; Reach charges 0 and 100. Halo 2 has no metagame block at all, and Halo 3 additionally carries `Minimum Death Time` (4.0) in Deprecated AI Globals, which ODST dropped entirely.

A NEGATIVE Friendly Death Point Count is the untested half: if the engine subtracts the value, negating it turns a marine's death into a gain. Not confirmed in game.

Sprint Speed.desc: Sprint faster. Tunes the base sprint speed from Options with an operator (+/-/*/=) in the patcher. Halo 1 sprint maps only.

Sprint Duration.desc: Sprint longer before it runs out. Tunes the base duration with an operator (+/-/*/=) in the patcher. Halo 1 sprint maps only.

Sprint Cooldown.desc: Shorter wait between sprints. Tunes the base cooldown with an operator (-x or *0.x to cut it) in the patcher. Halo 1 sprint maps only.

Sprint.desc: Unlock sprinting for the rest of the run (press the flashlight key). Halo 1 sprint maps only.

Overshield Strength.desc: A stronger overshield. Tunes the base multiplier from Options with an operator (+/-/*/=) in the patcher. Halo 1 ability maps only.

Regeneration Amount.desc: Regenerate more health per use. Tunes the base percentage with an operator (+/-/*/=) in the patcher. Halo 1 ability maps only.

Regeneration Speed.desc: How quickly the Regeneration ability heals you.
Regeneration Speed.debug_desc: Tunes the base duration with an operator (-x or *0.x to shorten it). Halo 1 ability maps only.

Camo Duration.desc: Stay invisible longer. Tunes the base camo duration with an operator (+/-/*/=) in the patcher. Halo 1 ability maps only.

Camo Cooldown.desc: Shorter wait between camo uses. Tunes the base cooldown with an operator (-x or *0.x to cut it) in the patcher. Halo 1 ability maps only.

Magnetism.desc: How hard your aim is pulled toward a target.
Magnetism.debug_desc:
`Magnetism Angle` and `Magnetism Range` are the pull on your reticle near a target, with `Magnetism Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) and Reach's `Magnetism Near Falloff Range` shaping where it fades. One decision, one input.

**Halo 2 declares this pair TWICE** (weap root 0x19C and 0x210) and the first is a different, mostly-zero field -- reading it makes Halo 2 look like it barely uses magnetism. The real pair is the second, next to Autoaim, so every Halo 2 row here is pinned to `nth: 1`. Every other game states nth 0 explicitly, because a gamed value falls back to the nearest EARLIER game and Halo 3 would otherwise inherit Halo 2's 1.

This is the weapon's own magnetism. The general Magnetism card is a different thing -- matg's Magnetism Friction and Adhesion, the controller-level aim friction that applies to everything.

Autoaim.desc: How hard the game steers your shots onto a target.
Autoaim.debug_desc:
`Autoaim Angle` is the cone the game will bend a shot into, `Autoaim Range` how far out it does so, and `Autoaim Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) where that help starts tapering off. All three are one decision -- how much the game shoots for you -- so they share one input.

Autoaim is the shot bending toward the target; Magnetism is your reticle being pulled. They are separate fields and separate cards.

Shipped values differ wildly by weapon and game: the Halo 3 assault rifle is 5deg/15 with falloff 7.5, the sniper 1deg/10, and Reach's sniper 0.8deg/20. Cutting these to 0 removes aim assist entirely, which is the harder direction.

Rider Damage.desc: How much of this weapon's damage reaches someone sitting in a vehicle.
Rider Damage.debug_desc:
The three `Rider ... Damage Scale` fields on the weapon's damage tag, moved together because they are one question split by how the damage arrives: `Direct` when the shot hits the rider, `Maximum`/`Minimum Transfer` when it hits the vehicle and passes through.

The split is visible in the shipped values from Halo 3 on: bullet weapons run Direct 1 and explosives Direct 0 -- a rocket does not hit the rider, it transfers (the Halo 3 and ODST rocket carries Minimum Transfer 3). Halo 2 is the odd one out and sets Direct 1 on rockets and needler too, plus fractional 0.75 on both plasma weapons.

**Not offered in Reach.** The fields still exist there but do nothing -- tested in-game on Tip of the Spear, and Assembly documents them as deprecated in Reach. Halo 2 is confirmed working; Halo 3 and ODST use the same names at the same offsets (0x44/0x48/0x4C). Halo 1 has no rider fields at all.

Applied to every damage tag the weapon owns, not one hand-picked tag: the Needler also supercombines, the plasma pistol also fires an overcharged bolt, and the flak round has an impact as well as an explosion. Feedback tags -- trigger kick, overheat, misfire, detach -- are left out, since nothing rides them.

Raising these makes the weapon better at killing drivers and gunners, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Weapon Swap Speed.desc: How fast you bring this weapon up and put it away. *0.5 is twice as fast.
Weapon Swap Speed.debug_desc:
Scales the `ready` and `put_away` first-person ANIMATIONS -- which is what weapon swap speed actually is. No weapon field drives it: `Ready Time` is non-zero on three weapons in Halo 3 and one in Reach (which is why testing it in Halo 2 showed nothing), `Weapon Ready-For-Use Time` on three, and ODST's promisingly-named `Weapon Ready 1st Person Animation Playback Scale` on none at all.

Measured lengths, at 30fps: Halo 3's assault rifle readies in 20 frames (0.67s) and stows in 6 (0.20s); the battle rifle 19/4; the shotgun 23/7; Halo 2's SMG 20/10. A swap plays the outgoing weapon's put_away and the incoming weapon's ready, so scaling both halves is what makes the whole exchange faster.

Same machinery as Reload Time -- the animation graph selects actions by label name, so this is the same code matching `ready`/`put_away` instead of `reload`. Halo Reach has no jmad layout yet, so it is not offered there (its Reload Time cards do not cover Reach either).

Melee Seeking.desc: How generously your melee swing snaps onto a target.
Melee Seeking.debug_desc:
The melee damage pyramid: `Damage Pyramid Angles` y and p are the cone your swing sweeps (yaw and pitch), `Damage Pyramid Depth` how far in front of you it reaches.

Reach MOVED these into a `Melee Damage Parameters` block rather than deleting them, so the card carries a per-game block instead of needing a separate card. Halo 1 has none of these fields at all.

Reach also re-tuned them: Halo 2 through ODST ship a wide, flat 12.512 x 6.062 at depth 0.6, while Reach squares it off to 9.211 x 9.211 -- narrower horizontally, much taller. Outliers worth knowing: the Energy Blade at 24.046 x 13.817 depth 0.9, the ODST Gravity Hammer / Flamethrower / turrets at 11.459 x 11.459 depth 0.8, Reach's Gravity Hammer at 20.854 x 15.352 depth 1.0, and Reach's Needler, which alone kept the old 12.512 x 6.062.

Widening the angles or deepening it makes melee more forgiving, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Marked `ignore` on this weapon: the pyramid is what a MELEE weapon is built around, and every gun merely carries one because the engine gives every weapon a melee. The card stays wired and verified here, so enabling it is a one-word edit, but only the Energy Blade and Gravity Hammer offer it.

Accuracy Penalties.desc: How badly your aim is thrown off after reloading or switching to this weapon.
Accuracy Penalties.debug_desc:
`Reload Penalty` and `Switch Penalty`, per barrel -- the accuracy hit applied after a reload and after bringing the weapon up. New in Reach; no earlier game has either field.

Measured on every weapon in all five games. Only seven Reach weapons carry values: assault rifle 2.5/1.0, DMR 2.4/1.0, needle rifle 2.35/0.8, magnum 2.35/1.0, plasma rifle 4.0/2.0, sniper rifle 2.5/0.89, spike rifle 2.5/1.0. The plasma rifle is the outlier at nearly double everything else on both.

Reach's other two accuracy penalties, `Zoom Penalty` and `Jump Penalty`, are 0 on every weapon and are not offered. The Forward/Sideways Movement penalties are a different mechanic entirely and live on the Movement Penalties card.

The card is offered only on the seven weapons that ship a value, because an operator on a stored 0 does nothing -- the rest of Reach's weapons have no penalty to scale.

Distribution Function.desc: Fans this weapon's shots out in a line instead of firing them all from one point.
Distribution Function.debug_desc:
Sets `Distribution Function` to `horizontal fan` and gives you `Distribution Angle` to tune. Both live per barrel (per trigger in Halo 1).

The angle is the whole effect: the function alone changes nothing you can see, so the set rides along with the angle row and only applies when you actually enter a value. Distribution Angle ships at 0 on every weapon in every game (81 of 81 read), hence zero_is 0.1 -- an operator works on 0.1 rather than multiplying 0 by something and still getting 0.

Despite the name the fan is NOT reliably horizontal -- tested in-game on the assault rifle, the line it spreads the shots along varies. What it does consistently is spread them along a line rather than from a point.

Only offered where the weapon already has a Projectiles Per Shot card: fanning a single projectile fans nothing, so the two belong together. `point` and `horizontal fan` are the only options every game shares; Reach adds `custom vectors` and `custom positions`, which need companion data to mean anything and are not offered.

Firing Noise.desc: How far away enemies hear you fire. Silent sneaks past them entirely; Shout pulls in the whole area.
Firing Noise.debug_desc:
The `Firing Noise` enum: a noise event raised for AI hearing, whose reach is bounded by the listener's own `Hearing Distance` (char; actr in Halo 1). The same enum drives biped/vehicle Constant Sound Volume and projectile Impact/Detonation Noise — one shared AI sense of hearing.

This card sets the weapon AND its projectile's Impact and Detonation Noise to the same level, because the two are heard in different places: the firing noise goes off at you, the impact noise goes off wherever the round lands. Silencing only the weapon still announced every shot at the far end.

Censused over 232 weapons in all five games, the names are not a ladder: Shout is the top tier (rockets, snipers, flak and AA cannons, Spartan Laser); Loud is the ordinary tier nearly everything ships with; Medium is the suppressed tier — ODST's automag and silenced SMG are the only two weapons anywhere that use it, plus Halo 1's sniper rifle; Silent is horns and cameras. Quiet is used by no shipped weapon in any game.

Applied by NAME because the codes moved: Halo 1 through ODST store Silent, Medium, Loud, Shout, Quiet; Reach stores Silent, Quiet, Medium, Shout, Loud. Halo 1 keeps the field per Trigger, every later game per Barrel. Reach also simply hears further — 100 to 200 world units against 40 to 50 in the older games.

Projectile.debug_desc:
`Maximum Range` and the velocity pair are the shot's reach and speed. The four damage-range fields are one row: Air and Water Damage Range are the same question asked of two media, and splitting them only invites setting them inconsistently.

GRAVITY. A second row appears wherever the projectile sets `Air Gravity Scale`. That matters most for the weapons which set it and NO air damage range at all -- measured, exactly the arcing launchers: Brute Shot (Halo 2 and 3), and Reach's Concussion Rifle, Grenade Launcher and Plasma Launcher. Their shot is a lobbed grenade whose flight gravity governs rather than a range falloff, so a Damage Range row alone would have given them a card that does nothing. Some ordinary weapons set air gravity too (Halo 1's pistol and shotgun at 1.0, Reach's magnum at 0.005) and get the row as well. Lower gravity flattens the arc and throws further.

Melee Damage.desc: Damage Lower Bound, Damage Upper Bound

desc_overrides.Halo 3: Damage Lower Bound, Damage Upper Bound. Uses two melee damage types, that are shared with different weapons.

Reload Time.desc: How long you spend reloading. *0.5 is twice as fast.
Reload Time.debug_desc: In the MCC every magazine-fed weapon reloads on its first-person animation — the tag-side reload timer is inert — so this scales the animation's length. Scales both Master Chief and Arbiter.

More Shooting.desc: How fast this weapon sprays while you hold the trigger.
More Shooting.debug_desc: Automatic, so Rounds Per Second is the real rate, ramping to Rounds Per Second Max while the trigger is held. Shots Per Fire is how many rounds one fire event sends; it ships at 1.

Fire Recovery Time.desc: Forces a pause between shots. Set a value to turn an automatic weapon semi-automatic.
Fire Recovery Time.debug_desc: The cooldown on trigger input, not the rate of fire itself. Automatic weapons ship this at 0, so multiplying does nothing — SET a value instead.

Fire Recovery Time.desc: How fast you can pull the trigger again. Lower is faster.

Error Angle.debug_desc:
The spread pair, plus `Deviation Angle`, which folds in here the same way it does on every other spread card.

**This is the card the zero-then-live sweep was built for.** The plasma pistol has had these fields since Halo 2 and ships them at 0 in every game up to ODST, so it never got a spread card -- its only one is Dual Weapon Error, which covers Halo 2/3/ODST. Reach fills them in (0.4 / 2.0, deviation 4.0) and nothing noticed, because a diff of NEW fields cannot see a field that was always there.

Reach declares Error Angle once, so nth 0 is correct here.

Magnetism.desc: How hard your aim is pulled toward a target.
Magnetism.debug_desc:
`Magnetism Angle` and `Magnetism Range` are the pull on your reticle near a target, with `Magnetism Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) and Reach's `Magnetism Near Falloff Range` shaping where it fades. One decision, one input.

**Halo 2 declares this pair TWICE** (weap root 0x19C and 0x210) and the first is a different, mostly-zero field -- reading it makes Halo 2 look like it barely uses magnetism. The real pair is the second, next to Autoaim, so every Halo 2 row here is pinned to `nth: 1`. Every other game states nth 0 explicitly, because a gamed value falls back to the nearest EARLIER game and Halo 3 would otherwise inherit Halo 2's 1.

This is the weapon's own magnetism. The general Magnetism card is a different thing -- matg's Magnetism Friction and Adhesion, the controller-level aim friction that applies to everything.

Autoaim.desc: How hard the game steers your shots onto a target.
Autoaim.debug_desc:
`Autoaim Angle` is the cone the game will bend a shot into, `Autoaim Range` how far out it does so, and `Autoaim Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) where that help starts tapering off. All three are one decision -- how much the game shoots for you -- so they share one input.

Autoaim is the shot bending toward the target; Magnetism is your reticle being pulled. They are separate fields and separate cards.

Shipped values differ wildly by weapon and game: the Halo 3 assault rifle is 5deg/15 with falloff 7.5, the sniper 1deg/10, and Reach's sniper 0.8deg/20. Cutting these to 0 removes aim assist entirely, which is the harder direction.

Weapon Swap Speed.desc: How fast you bring this weapon up and put it away. *0.5 is twice as fast.
Weapon Swap Speed.debug_desc:
Scales the `ready` and `put_away` first-person ANIMATIONS -- which is what weapon swap speed actually is. No weapon field drives it: `Ready Time` is non-zero on three weapons in Halo 3 and one in Reach (which is why testing it in Halo 2 showed nothing), `Weapon Ready-For-Use Time` on three, and ODST's promisingly-named `Weapon Ready 1st Person Animation Playback Scale` on none at all.

Measured lengths, at 30fps: Halo 3's assault rifle readies in 20 frames (0.67s) and stows in 6 (0.20s); the battle rifle 19/4; the shotgun 23/7; Halo 2's SMG 20/10. A swap plays the outgoing weapon's put_away and the incoming weapon's ready, so scaling both halves is what makes the whole exchange faster.

Same machinery as Reload Time -- the animation graph selects actions by label name, so this is the same code matching `ready`/`put_away` instead of `reload`. Halo Reach has no jmad layout yet, so it is not offered there (its Reload Time cards do not cover Reach either).

Reload Time.desc: How long you spend reloading. *0.5 is twice as fast.
Reload Time.debug_desc: In the MCC every magazine-fed weapon reloads on its first-person animation — the tag-side reload timer is inert — so this scales the animation's length. Scales both Master Chief and Arbiter.

Rider Damage.desc: How much of this weapon's damage reaches someone sitting in a vehicle.
Rider Damage.debug_desc:
The three `Rider ... Damage Scale` fields on the weapon's damage tag, moved together because they are one question split by how the damage arrives: `Direct` when the shot hits the rider, `Maximum`/`Minimum Transfer` when it hits the vehicle and passes through.

The split is visible in the shipped values from Halo 3 on: bullet weapons run Direct 1 and explosives Direct 0 -- a rocket does not hit the rider, it transfers (the Halo 3 and ODST rocket carries Minimum Transfer 3). Halo 2 is the odd one out and sets Direct 1 on rockets and needler too, plus fractional 0.75 on both plasma weapons.

**Not offered in Reach.** The fields still exist there but do nothing -- tested in-game on Tip of the Spear, and Assembly documents them as deprecated in Reach. Halo 2 is confirmed working; Halo 3 and ODST use the same names at the same offsets (0x44/0x48/0x4C). Halo 1 has no rider fields at all.

Applied to every damage tag the weapon owns, not one hand-picked tag: the Needler also supercombines, the plasma pistol also fires an overcharged bolt, and the flak round has an impact as well as an explosion. Feedback tags -- trigger kick, overheat, misfire, detach -- are left out, since nothing rides them.

Raising these makes the weapon better at killing drivers and gunners, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Melee Seeking.desc: How generously your melee swing snaps onto a target.
Melee Seeking.debug_desc:
The melee damage pyramid: `Damage Pyramid Angles` y and p are the cone your swing sweeps (yaw and pitch), `Damage Pyramid Depth` how far in front of you it reaches.

Reach MOVED these into a `Melee Damage Parameters` block rather than deleting them, so the card carries a per-game block instead of needing a separate card. Halo 1 has none of these fields at all.

Reach also re-tuned them: Halo 2 through ODST ship a wide, flat 12.512 x 6.062 at depth 0.6, while Reach squares it off to 9.211 x 9.211 -- narrower horizontally, much taller. Outliers worth knowing: the Energy Blade at 24.046 x 13.817 depth 0.9, the ODST Gravity Hammer / Flamethrower / turrets at 11.459 x 11.459 depth 0.8, Reach's Gravity Hammer at 20.854 x 15.352 depth 1.0, and Reach's Needler, which alone kept the old 12.512 x 6.062.

Widening the angles or deepening it makes melee more forgiving, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Marked `ignore` on this weapon: the pyramid is what a MELEE weapon is built around, and every gun merely carries one because the engine gives every weapon a melee. The card stays wired and verified here, so enabling it is a one-word edit, but only the Energy Blade and Gravity Hammer offer it.

Accuracy Penalties.desc: How badly your aim is thrown off after reloading or switching to this weapon.
Accuracy Penalties.debug_desc:
`Reload Penalty` and `Switch Penalty`, per barrel -- the accuracy hit applied after a reload and after bringing the weapon up. New in Reach; no earlier game has either field.

Measured on every weapon in all five games. Only seven Reach weapons carry values: assault rifle 2.5/1.0, DMR 2.4/1.0, needle rifle 2.35/0.8, magnum 2.35/1.0, plasma rifle 4.0/2.0, sniper rifle 2.5/0.89, spike rifle 2.5/1.0. The plasma rifle is the outlier at nearly double everything else on both.

Reach's other two accuracy penalties, `Zoom Penalty` and `Jump Penalty`, are 0 on every weapon and are not offered. The Forward/Sideways Movement penalties are a different mechanic entirely and live on the Movement Penalties card.

The card is offered only on the seven weapons that ship a value, because an operator on a stored 0 does nothing -- the rest of Reach's weapons have no penalty to scale.

This weapon ships BOTH penalties at 0, so it is marked `ignore` and stays out of the offer pool: an operator on a stored 0 does nothing, and a card that reads as broken is worse than no card. The wiring is here and verified, so enabling it later -- for a run that wants to IMPOSE a penalty with `=` -- is a one-word edit.

Distribution Function.desc: Fans this weapon's shots out in a line instead of firing them all from one point.
Distribution Function.debug_desc:
Sets `Distribution Function` to `horizontal fan` and gives you `Distribution Angle` to tune. Both live per barrel (per trigger in Halo 1).

The angle is the whole effect: the function alone changes nothing you can see, so the set rides along with the angle row and only applies when you actually enter a value. Distribution Angle ships at 0 on every weapon in every game (81 of 81 read), hence zero_is 0.1 -- an operator works on 0.1 rather than multiplying 0 by something and still getting 0.

Despite the name the fan is NOT reliably horizontal -- tested in-game on the assault rifle, the line it spreads the shots along varies. What it does consistently is spread them along a line rather than from a point.

Only offered where the weapon already has a Projectiles Per Shot card: fanning a single projectile fans nothing, so the two belong together. `point` and `horizontal fan` are the only options every game shares; Reach adds `custom vectors` and `custom positions`, which need companion data to mean anything and are not offered.

Target Tracking.desc: How long this weapon takes to lock on, and how long the lock survives.
Target Tracking.debug_desc:
Reach's `Target Tracking` block on the weapon: Acquire Time is how long you must hold the target before the lock takes, Grace Time how long a lock survives losing it, Decay Time how long it takes to bleed away after that.

New in Reach -- no earlier game has the block. Only 11 weapon tags populate it and four belong to weapons the player gets cards for: needler and plasma pistol carry Grace/Decay only (their soft tracking has no acquire delay), while rocket launcher (1.5s) and plasma launcher (0.5s) carry a real Acquire Time -- that is the wait before the reticle locks.

Separate from Homing, which is how hard the round steers once it is already in the air.

Firing Noise.desc: How far away enemies hear you fire. Silent sneaks past them entirely; Shout pulls in the whole area.
Firing Noise.debug_desc:
The `Firing Noise` enum: a noise event raised for AI hearing, whose reach is bounded by the listener's own `Hearing Distance` (char; actr in Halo 1). The same enum drives biped/vehicle Constant Sound Volume and projectile Impact/Detonation Noise — one shared AI sense of hearing.

This card sets the weapon AND its projectile's Impact and Detonation Noise to the same level, because the two are heard in different places: the firing noise goes off at you, the impact noise goes off wherever the round lands. Silencing only the weapon still announced every shot at the far end.

Censused over 232 weapons in all five games, the names are not a ladder: Shout is the top tier (rockets, snipers, flak and AA cannons, Spartan Laser); Loud is the ordinary tier nearly everything ships with; Medium is the suppressed tier — ODST's automag and silenced SMG are the only two weapons anywhere that use it, plus Halo 1's sniper rifle; Silent is horns and cameras. Quiet is used by no shipped weapon in any game.

Applied by NAME because the codes moved: Halo 1 through ODST store Silent, Medium, Loud, Shout, Quiet; Reach stores Silent, Quiet, Medium, Shout, Loud. Halo 1 keeps the field per Trigger, every later game per Barrel. Reach also simply hears further — 100 to 200 world units against 40 to 50 in the older games.

Homing (Charged).desc: How hard this weapon's shots bend toward what you aimed at.
Homing (Charged).debug_desc:
The projectile's `Guided Angular Velocity` pair (plus At Rest, and the Outer Range Error Radius) -- how sharply a round already in flight can steer. This is NOT the lock-on: acquiring the target is `Target Tracking` on the weapon, its own card in Reach.

Reach keeps these fields exactly where Halo 3 had them, so it only needed adding to the card -- but its tag paths differ (Halo 3 nests needler_shard and flak_bolt one folder deeper), which is why Reach carries its own tag rather than inheriting.

Higher steers harder. Push it far enough and shots curve around cover.

More Shooting.desc: How fast this weapon sprays while you hold the trigger.

Fire Recovery Time.desc: Forces a pause between shots. Set a value to turn an automatic weapon semi-automatic.

Ramp Up.desc: How long the weapon takes to spin up to full rate, and to wind back down.
Ramp Up.debug_desc:
`Acceleration Time` is how long the weapon takes to reach its full rate of fire, `Deceleration Time` how long it takes to wind back down. Per barrel.

No card clamps Deceleration against Acceleration any more -- the constraint was removed on 2026-08-26 for retesting. The reasoning behind it was that guns spin up slowly and spin down fast, which holds for the plasma rifle, brute plasma rifle and needler, but is NOT universal: measuring every weapon that sets these fields disproves the stronger claim this text used to make: six weapon-games ship the OPPOSITE. Halo 3 and ODST's machinegun turret and plasma cannon both run 1.25 up / 2.0 down, Reach's plasma launcher 0.7 / 1.0, and Reach's spike rifle 0.0 / 0.2 -- it has no spin-up at all and still takes time to stop.

So the weapons that ship deceleration above acceleration deliberately carry NO constraint: clamping them would quietly rewrite their vanilla behaviour the first time the card was patched.

Also note Reach's stringid Rate Of Fire Acceleration/Deceleration fields are dead -- these numeric Time fields are the ones that carry the values.

More Shooting.desc: How fast this weapon sprays while you hold the trigger.

Fire Recovery Time.desc: Forces a pause between shots. Set a value to turn an automatic weapon semi-automatic.

Ramp Up.desc: How long the weapon takes to spin up to full rate, and to wind back down.
Ramp Up.debug_desc:
`Acceleration Time` is how long the weapon takes to reach its full rate of fire, `Deceleration Time` how long it takes to wind back down. Per barrel.

Projectiles Per Shot.desc: For every projectily, fire this many

Recoil.desc: How far your aim climbs with each shot.

Raising these makes the weapon better at killing drivers and gunners, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Target Tracking.desc: How long this weapon takes to lock on, and how long the lock survives.
Target Tracking.debug_desc:
Reach's `Target Tracking` block on the weapon: Acquire Time is how long you must hold the target before the lock takes, Grace Time how long a lock survives losing it, Decay Time how long it takes to bleed away after that.

New in Reach -- no earlier game has the block. Only 11 weapon tags populate it and four belong to weapons the player gets cards for: needler and plasma pistol carry Grace/Decay only (their soft tracking has no acquire delay), while rocket launcher (1.5s) and plasma launcher (0.5s) carry a real Acquire Time -- that is the wait before the reticle locks.

Separate from Homing, which is how hard the round steers once it is already in the air.

Homing.desc: How hard this weapon's shots bend toward what you aimed at.
Homing.debug_desc:

Reach keeps these fields exactly where Halo 3 had them, so it only needed adding to the card -- but its tag paths differ (Halo 3 nests needler_shard and flak_bolt one folder deeper), which is why Reach carries its own tag rather than inheriting.

Higher steers harder. Push it far enough and shots curve around cover.

Firing Noise.desc: How far away enemies hear you fire. Silent sneaks past them entirely; Shout pulls in the whole area.

This card sets the weapon AND its projectile's Impact and Detonation Noise to the same level, because the two are heard in different places: the firing noise goes off at you, the impact noise goes off wherever the round lands. Silencing only the weapon still announced every shot at the far end.

Projectile.debug_desc:

That matters most for the weapons which set it and NO air damage range at all -- measured, exactly the arcing launchers: Brute Shot (Halo 2 and 3), and Reach's Concussion Rifle, Grenade Launcher and Plasma Launcher. Reload Time.desc: How long you spend reloading. *0.5 is twice as fast.

Projectiles Per Shot.desc: For every projectily, fire this many

Magnetism.desc: How hard your aim is pulled toward a target.
Magnetism.debug_desc:
`Magnetism Angle` and `Magnetism Range` are the pull on your reticle near a target, with `Magnetism Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) and Reach's `Magnetism Near Falloff Range` shaping where it fades. One decision, one input.

**Halo 2 declares this pair TWICE** (weap root 0x19C and 0x210) and the first is a different, mostly-zero field -- reading it makes Halo 2 look like it barely uses magnetism. The real pair is the second, next to Autoaim, so every Halo 2 row here is pinned to `nth: 1`. Every other game states nth 0 explicitly, because a gamed value falls back to the nearest EARLIER game and Halo 3 would otherwise inherit Halo 2's 1.

This is the weapon's own magnetism. The general Magnetism card is a different thing -- matg's Magnetism Friction and Adhesion, the controller-level aim friction that applies to everything.

Autoaim.desc: How hard the game steers your shots onto a target.
Autoaim.debug_desc:

Shipped values differ wildly by weapon and game: the Halo 3 assault rifle is 5deg/15 with falloff 7.5, the sniper 1deg/10, and Reach's sniper 0.8deg/20. Cutting these to 0 removes aim assist entirely, which is the harder direction.

Rider Damage.desc: How much of this weapon's damage reaches someone sitting in a vehicle.
Rider Damage.debug_desc:
The three `Rider ... Damage Scale` fields on the weapon's damage tag, moved together because they are one question split by how the damage arrives: `Direct` when the shot hits the rider, `Maximum`/`Minimum Transfer` when it hits the vehicle and passes through.

The split is visible in the shipped values from Halo 3 on: bullet weapons run Direct 1 and explosives Direct 0 -- a rocket does not hit the rider, it transfers (the Halo 3 and ODST rocket carries Minimum Transfer 3). Halo 2 is the odd one out and sets Direct 1 on rockets and needler too, plus fractional 0.75 on both plasma weapons.

Applied to every damage tag the weapon owns, not one hand-picked tag: the Needler also supercombines, the plasma pistol also fires an overcharged bolt, and the flak round has an impact as well as an explosion. Feedback tags -- trigger kick, overheat, misfire, detach -- are left out, since nothing rides them.

Raising these makes the weapon better at killing drivers and gunners, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Weapon Swap Speed.desc: How fast you bring this weapon up and put it away. *0.5 is twice as fast.
Weapon Swap Speed.debug_desc:

Same machinery as Reload Time -- the animation graph selects actions by label name, so this is the same code matching `ready`/`put_away` instead of `reload`. Halo Reach has no jmad layout yet, so it is not offered there (its Reload Time cards do not cover Reach either).

The card is offered only on the seven weapons that ship a value, because an operator on a stored 0 does nothing -- the rest of Reach's weapons have no penalty to scale.

This weapon ships BOTH penalties at 0, so it is marked `ignore` and stays out of the offer pool: an operator on a stored 0 does nothing, and a card that reads as broken is worse than no card. The wiring is here and verified, so enabling it later -- for a run that wants to IMPOSE a penalty with `=` -- is a one-word edit.

Melee Seeking.desc: How generously your melee swing snaps onto a target.

Distribution Function.desc: Fans this weapon's shots out in a line instead of firing them all from one point.
Distribution Function.debug_desc:

The angle is the whole effect: the function alone changes nothing you can see, so the set rides along with the angle row and only applies when you actually enter a value. Distribution Angle ships at 0 on every weapon in every game (81 of 81 read), hence zero_is 0.1 -- an operator works on 0.1 rather than multiplying 0 by something and still getting 0.

Despite the name the fan is NOT reliably horizontal -- tested in-game on the assault rifle, the line it spreads the shots along varies. What it does consistently is spread them along a line rather than from a point.

Firing Noise.desc: How far away enemies hear you fire. Silent sneaks past them entirely; Shout pulls in the whole area.
Firing Noise.debug_desc:

Heat Recovery.desc: Threshold for being useable after Overheating and Heat Loss

Misfire.desc: When Misifirng starts and how likely it is

More Shooting.desc: How fast this weapon sprays while you hold the trigger.
More Shooting.debug_desc: Automatic, so Rounds Per Second is the real rate, ramping to Rounds Per Second Max while the trigger is held. Shots Per Fire is how many rounds one fire event sends; it ships at 1.

Fire Recovery Time.desc: Forces a pause between shots. Set a value to turn an automatic weapon semi-automatic.
Fire Recovery Time.debug_desc: The cooldown on trigger input, not the rate of fire itself. Automatic weapons ship this at 0, so multiplying does nothing — SET a value instead.

Ramp Up.desc: How long the weapon takes to spin up to full rate, and to wind back down.
Ramp Up.debug_desc:
`Acceleration Time` is how long the weapon takes to reach its full rate of fire, `Deceleration Time` how long it takes to wind back down. Per barrel.

No card clamps Deceleration against Acceleration any more -- the constraint was removed on 2026-08-26 for retesting. The reasoning behind it was that guns spin up slowly and spin down fast, which holds for the plasma rifle, brute plasma rifle and needler, but is NOT universal: measuring every weapon that sets these fields disproves the stronger claim this text used to make: six weapon-games ship the OPPOSITE. Projectiles Per Shot.desc: Projectiles per shot

Per Round.desc: Heat and Age generated per shot

Melee Damage.desc: Damage Lower Bound, Damage Upper Bound. Uses a melee damage type, that is shared with different weapons.

Magnetism.desc: How hard your aim is pulled toward a target.
Magnetism.debug_desc:

Rider Damage.desc: How much of this weapon's damage reaches someone sitting in a vehicle.
Rider Damage.debug_desc:
The three `Rider ... Damage Scale` fields on the weapon's damage tag, moved together because they are one question split by how the damage arrives: `Direct` when the shot hits the rider, `Maximum`/`Minimum Transfer` when it hits the vehicle and passes through.

The split is visible in the shipped values from Halo 3 on: bullet weapons run Direct 1 and explosives Direct 0 -- a rocket does not hit the rider, it transfers (the Halo 3 and ODST rocket carries Minimum Transfer 3). Halo 2 is the odd one out and sets Direct 1 on rockets and needler too, plus fractional 0.75 on both plasma weapons.

Raising these makes the weapon better at killing drivers and gunners, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Recoil.desc: How far your aim climbs with each shot.

More Shooting.desc: Turns one shot per pull into a burst. Raise Shots Per Fire for more rounds, Rounds Per Second to space them out.
More Shooting.debug_desc: This weapon sends one round per trigger pull, so Rounds Per Second does nothing until Shots Per Fire is above 1 — it is what spaces the rounds inside a single pull. How fast you can pull the trigger is Fire Recovery Time, on its own card.

Fire Recovery Time.desc: How fast you can pull the trigger again. Lower is faster.
Fire Recovery Time.debug_desc: The cooldown on trigger input after a shot. On a one-round-per-pull weapon this IS its rate of fire, so lowering it is the way to speed the weapon up.

Projectiles Per Shot.desc: For every projectily, fire this many

Error Angle.desc: Spread of the shot, Minimum Error and Maximum Error

Magnetism.desc: How hard your aim is pulled toward a target.
Magnetism.debug_desc:
`Magnetism Angle` and `Magnetism Range` are the pull on your reticle near a target, with `Magnetism Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) and Reach's `Magnetism Near Falloff Range` shaping where it fades. One decision, one input.

**Halo 2 declares this pair TWICE** (weap root 0x19C and 0x210) and the first is a different, mostly-zero field -- reading it makes Halo 2 look like it barely uses magnetism. The real pair is the second, next to Autoaim, so every Halo 2 row here is pinned to `nth: 1`. Every other game states nth 0 explicitly, because a gamed value falls back to the nearest EARLIER game and Halo 3 would otherwise inherit Halo 2's 1.

This is the weapon's own magnetism. The general Magnetism card is a different thing -- matg's Magnetism Friction and Adhesion, the controller-level aim friction that applies to everything.

Autoaim.desc: How hard the game steers your shots onto a target.
Autoaim.debug_desc:
`Autoaim Angle` is the cone the game will bend a shot into, `Autoaim Range` how far out it does so, and `Autoaim Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) where that help starts tapering off. All three are one decision -- how much the game shoots for you -- so they share one input.

Autoaim is the shot bending toward the target; Magnetism is your reticle being pulled. They are separate fields and separate cards.

Shipped values differ wildly by weapon and game: the Halo 3 assault rifle is 5deg/15 with falloff 7.5, the sniper 1deg/10, and Reach's sniper 0.8deg/20. Cutting these to 0 removes aim assist entirely, which is the harder direction.

Rider Damage.desc: How much of this weapon's damage reaches someone sitting in a vehicle.
Rider Damage.debug_desc:
The three `Rider ... Damage Scale` fields on the weapon's damage tag, moved together because they are one question split by how the damage arrives: `Direct` when the shot hits the rider, `Maximum`/`Minimum Transfer` when it hits the vehicle and passes through.

The split is visible in the shipped values from Halo 3 on: bullet weapons run Direct 1 and explosives Direct 0 -- a rocket does not hit the rider, it transfers (the Halo 3 and ODST rocket carries Minimum Transfer 3). Halo 2 is the odd one out and sets Direct 1 on rockets and needler too, plus fractional 0.75 on both plasma weapons.

**Not offered in Reach.** The fields still exist there but do nothing -- tested in-game on Tip of the Spear, and Assembly documents them as deprecated in Reach. Halo 2 is confirmed working; Halo 3 and ODST use the same names at the same offsets (0x44/0x48/0x4C). Halo 1 has no rider fields at all.

Applied to every damage tag the weapon owns, not one hand-picked tag: the Needler also supercombines, the plasma pistol also fires an overcharged bolt, and the flak round has an impact as well as an explosion. Feedback tags -- trigger kick, overheat, misfire, detach -- are left out, since nothing rides them.

Raising these makes the weapon better at killing drivers and gunners, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Melee Seeking.desc: How generously your melee swing snaps onto a target.
Melee Seeking.debug_desc:
The melee damage pyramid: `Damage Pyramid Angles` y and p are the cone your swing sweeps (yaw and pitch), `Damage Pyramid Depth` how far in front of you it reaches.

Reach MOVED these into a `Melee Damage Parameters` block rather than deleting them, so the card carries a per-game block instead of needing a separate card. Halo 1 has none of these fields at all.

Reach also re-tuned them: Halo 2 through ODST ship a wide, flat 12.512 x 6.062 at depth 0.6, while Reach squares it off to 9.211 x 9.211 -- narrower horizontally, much taller. Outliers worth knowing: the Energy Blade at 24.046 x 13.817 depth 0.9, the ODST Gravity Hammer / Flamethrower / turrets at 11.459 x 11.459 depth 0.8, Reach's Gravity Hammer at 20.854 x 15.352 depth 1.0, and Reach's Needler, which alone kept the old 12.512 x 6.062.

Widening the angles or deepening it makes melee more forgiving, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Marked `ignore` on this weapon: the pyramid is what a MELEE weapon is built around, and every gun merely carries one because the engine gives every weapon a melee. The card stays wired and verified here, so enabling it is a one-word edit, but only the Energy Blade and Gravity Hammer offer it.

Distribution Function.desc: Fans this weapon's shots out in a line instead of firing them all from one point.
Distribution Function.debug_desc:
Sets `Distribution Function` to `horizontal fan` and gives you `Distribution Angle` to tune. Both live per barrel (per trigger in Halo 1).

The angle is the whole effect: the function alone changes nothing you can see, so the set rides along with the angle row and only applies when you actually enter a value. Distribution Angle ships at 0 on every weapon in every game (81 of 81 read), hence zero_is 0.1 -- an operator works on 0.1 rather than multiplying 0 by something and still getting 0.

Despite the name the fan is NOT reliably horizontal -- tested in-game on the assault rifle, the line it spreads the shots along varies. What it does consistently is spread them along a line rather than from a point.

Only offered where the weapon already has a Projectiles Per Shot card: fanning a single projectile fans nothing, so the two belong together. `point` and `horizontal fan` are the only options every game shares; Reach adds `custom vectors` and `custom positions`, which need companion data to mean anything and are not offered.

Firing Noise.desc: How far away enemies hear you fire. Silent sneaks past them entirely; Shout pulls in the whole area.
Firing Noise.debug_desc:
The `Firing Noise` enum: a noise event raised for AI hearing, whose reach is bounded by the listener's own `Hearing Distance` (char; actr in Halo 1). The same enum drives biped/vehicle Constant Sound Volume and projectile Impact/Detonation Noise — one shared AI sense of hearing.

This card sets the weapon AND its projectile's Impact and Detonation Noise to the same level, because the two are heard in different places: the firing noise goes off at you, the impact noise goes off wherever the round lands. Silencing only the weapon still announced every shot at the far end.

Censused over 232 weapons in all five games, the names are not a ladder: Shout is the top tier (rockets, snipers, flak and AA cannons, Spartan Laser); Loud is the ordinary tier nearly everything ships with; Medium is the suppressed tier — ODST's automag and silenced SMG are the only two weapons anywhere that use it, plus Halo 1's sniper rifle; Silent is horns and cameras. Quiet is used by no shipped weapon in any game.

Applied by NAME because the codes moved: Halo 1 through ODST store Silent, Medium, Loud, Shout, Quiet; Reach stores Silent, Quiet, Medium, Shout, Loud. Halo 1 keeps the field per Trigger, every later game per Barrel. Reach also simply hears further — 100 to 200 world units against 40 to 50 in the older games.

Projectile.debug_desc:
`Maximum Range` and the velocity pair are the shot's reach and speed. The four damage-range fields are one row: Air and Water Damage Range are the same question asked of two media, and splitting them only invites setting them inconsistently.

Some ordinary weapons set air gravity too (Halo 1's pistol and shotgun at 1.0, Reach's magnum at 0.005) and get the row as well. Lower gravity flattens the arc and throws further.

Beam Damage.desc: How hard the beam hits. In Halo 2 it also arms every Sentinel shooting at you.
Beam Damage.debug_desc: Damage Lower/Upper Bound. In Halo 2 the player's Sentinel Beam is the exact same weapon the Sentinel enemy fires — one damage tag — so buffing it buffs the enemies too. That is why the Sentinel enemy's own Beam Damage card is Halo 1 only.

Melee Damage.desc: How hard your melee hits.
Melee Damage.debug_desc: Damage Lower/Upper Bound on a melee damage type shared with several weapons. The damage type switches between Halo 2 and Halo 3.

desc_overrides.Halo 3: Damage Lower Bound, Damage Upper Bound. Uses a melee damage type, that is shared with different weapons. The damage type switches from H2 to H3.

Zoom.desc: Magnification Levels, Magnification Range. The Sentinel Beam has no vanilla scope - give it one by setting Magnification Levels above 0.

Heat Recovery.desc: Threshold for being useable after Overheating and Heat Loss

Per Round.desc: Heat per Round, Age (battery drain) per Round

More Shooting.desc: How fast this weapon sprays while you hold the trigger.
More Shooting.debug_desc: Automatic, so Rounds Per Second is the real rate, ramping to Rounds Per Second Max while the trigger is held. Shots Per Fire is how many rounds one fire event sends; it ships at 1.

Fire Recovery Time.desc: Forces a pause between shots. Set a value to turn an automatic weapon semi-automatic.
Fire Recovery Time.debug_desc: The cooldown on trigger input, not the rate of fire itself. Automatic weapons ship this at 0, so multiplying does nothing — SET a value instead.

Weapon Swap Speed.debug_desc:

Slice Damage.desc: Normal Swing damage. Uses a melee damage type, that is shared with different weapons.

Strike Damage.desc: Damage of the depleted sword. Uses a melee damage type, that is shared with different weapons.

Lunge Range.desc: How far you travel to land the hit.
Lunge Range.debug_desc: Reach's `Maximum Lunge Range` in `Melee Damage Parameters`: the distance you actually cover lunging at a target.\n\nThis card used to carry `Autoaim Range` too -- how far the game helps the swing find a target -- but that field now belongs to this weapon's own Autoaim card, and two cards writing one field compound. Grenade Damage.desc: Damage Lower Bound, Damage Upper Bound

Maximum Count.desc: Maximum amount of Grenade by Type

Halo 3 and ODST's machinegun turret and plasma cannon both run 1.25 up / 2.0 down, Reach's plasma launcher 0.7 / 1.0, and Reach's spike rifle 0.0 / 0.2 -- it has no spin-up at all and still takes time to stop.

So the weapons that ship deceleration above acceleration deliberately carry NO constraint: clamping them would quietly rewrite their vanilla behaviour the first time the card was patched.

Melee Seeking.desc: How generously your melee swing snaps onto a target.
Melee Seeking.debug_desc:

Reach also re-tuned them: Halo 2 through ODST ship a wide, flat 12.512 x 6.062 at depth 0.6, while Reach squares it off to 9.211 x 9.211 -- narrower horizontally, much taller. Accuracy Penalties.desc: How badly your aim is thrown off after reloading or switching to this weapon.
Accuracy Penalties.debug_desc:
`Reload Penalty` and `Switch Penalty`, per barrel -- the accuracy hit applied after a reload and after bringing the weapon up. New in Reach; no earlier game has either field.

Measured on every weapon in all five games. Only seven Reach weapons carry values: assault rifle 2.5/1.0, DMR 2.4/1.0, needle rifle 2.35/0.8, magnum 2.35/1.0, plasma rifle 4.0/2.0, sniper rifle 2.5/0.89, spike rifle 2.5/1.0. The plasma rifle is the outlier at nearly double everything else on both.

Reach's other two accuracy penalties, `Zoom Penalty` and `Jump Penalty`, are 0 on every weapon and are not offered. The Forward/Sideways Movement penalties are a different mechanic entirely and live on the Movement Penalties card.

The card is offered only on the seven weapons that ship a value, because an operator on a stored 0 does nothing -- the rest of Reach's weapons have no penalty to scale.

Halo 1 keeps the field per Trigger, every later game per Barrel. Reach also simply hears further — 100 to 200 world units against 40 to 50 in the older games.

Melee Damage.desc: Lower Bound and Upper Bound Damage. Shared with other weapons.

Projectile.desc: Range and speed of the spikes
Projectile.debug_desc:
`Maximum Range` and the velocity pair are the shot's reach and speed. The four damage-range fields are one row: Air and Water Damage Range are the same question asked of two media, and splitting them only invites setting them inconsistently.

GRAVITY. A second row appears wherever the projectile sets `Air Gravity Scale`. That matters most for the weapons which set it and NO air damage range at all -- measured, exactly the arcing launchers: Brute Shot (Halo 2 and 3), and Reach's Concussion Rifle, Grenade Launcher and Plasma Launcher. Magazine.desc: Magazine and carried ammo

Reload Time.desc: How long you spend reloading. *0.5 is twice as fast.
Reload Time.debug_desc: In the MCC every magazine-fed weapon reloads on its first-person animation — the tag-side reload timer is inert — so this scales the animation's length. Scales both Master Chief and Arbiter.

More Shooting.desc: How fast this weapon sprays while you hold the trigger.
More Shooting.debug_desc: Automatic, so Rounds Per Second is the real rate, ramping to Rounds Per Second Max while the trigger is held. Shots Per Fire is how many rounds one fire event sends; it ships at 1.

Fire Recovery Time.desc: Forces a pause between shots. Set a value to turn an automatic weapon semi-automatic.
Fire Recovery Time.debug_desc: The cooldown on trigger input, not the rate of fire itself. Automatic weapons ship this at 0, so multiplying does nothing — SET a value instead.

Magnetism.desc: How hard your aim is pulled toward a target.
Magnetism.debug_desc:
`Magnetism Angle` and `Magnetism Range` are the pull on your reticle near a target, with `Magnetism Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) and Reach's `Magnetism Near Falloff Range` shaping where it fades. One decision, one input.

**Halo 2 declares this pair TWICE** (weap root 0x19C and 0x210) and the first is a different, mostly-zero field -- reading it makes Halo 2 look like it barely uses magnetism. The real pair is the second, next to Autoaim, so every Halo 2 row here is pinned to `nth: 1`. Every other game states nth 0 explicitly, because a gamed value falls back to the nearest EARLIER game and Halo 3 would otherwise inherit Halo 2's 1.

This is the weapon's own magnetism. The general Magnetism card is a different thing -- matg's Magnetism Friction and Adhesion, the controller-level aim friction that applies to everything.

Autoaim.desc: How hard the game steers your shots onto a target.
Autoaim.debug_desc:
`Autoaim Angle` is the cone the game will bend a shot into, `Autoaim Range` how far out it does so, and `Autoaim Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) where that help starts tapering off. All three are one decision -- how much the game shoots for you -- so they share one input.

Autoaim is the shot bending toward the target; Magnetism is your reticle being pulled. They are separate fields and separate cards.

Shipped values differ wildly by weapon and game: the Halo 3 assault rifle is 5deg/15 with falloff 7.5, the sniper 1deg/10, and Reach's sniper 0.8deg/20. Cutting these to 0 removes aim assist entirely, which is the harder direction.

Weapon Swap Speed.desc: How fast you bring this weapon up and put it away. *0.5 is twice as fast.
Weapon Swap Speed.debug_desc:

No weapon field drives it: `Ready Time` is non-zero on three weapons in Halo 3 and one in Reach (which is why testing it in Halo 2 showed nothing), `Weapon Ready-For-Use Time` on three, and ODST's promisingly-named `Weapon Ready 1st Person Animation Playback Scale` on none at all.

Measured lengths, at 30fps: Halo 3's assault rifle readies in 20 frames (0.67s) and stows in 6 (0.20s); the battle rifle 19/4; the shotgun 23/7; Halo 2's SMG 20/10. A swap plays the outgoing weapon's put_away and the incoming weapon's ready, so scaling both halves is what makes the whole exchange faster.

Same machinery as Reload Time -- the animation graph selects actions by label name, so this is the same code matching `ready`/`put_away` instead of `reload`. Halo Reach has no jmad layout yet, so it is not offered there (its Reload Time cards do not cover Reach either).

Zoom.desc: How far this weapon zooms — set Magnification Levels above 0 to give it a scope.
Zoom.debug_desc:

Melee Damage.desc: Lower Bound and Upper Bound Damage. One effect shared with other weapons.

Hammer Radius.desc: Blast radius of the gravity blast

Lunge Range.desc: How far you travel to land the hit.
Lunge Range.debug_desc: Reach's `Maximum Lunge Range` in `Melee Damage Parameters`: the distance you actually cover lunging at a target.\n\nThis card used to carry `Autoaim Range` too -- how far the game helps the swing find a target -- but that field now belongs to this weapon's own Autoaim card, and two cards writing one field compound. Halo 2 is the odd one out and sets Direct 1 on rockets and needler too, plus fractional 0.75 on both plasma weapons.

**Not offered in Reach.** The fields still exist there but do nothing -- tested in-game on Tip of the Spear, and Assembly documents them as deprecated in Reach. Halo 2 is confirmed working; Halo 3 and ODST use the same names at the same offsets (0x44/0x48/0x4C). Halo 1 has no rider fields at all.

Applied to every damage tag the weapon owns, not one hand-picked tag: the Needler also supercombines, the plasma pistol also fires an overcharged bolt, and the flak round has an impact as well as an explosion. Feedback tags -- trigger kick, overheat, misfire, detach -- are left out, since nothing rides them.

Heat Recovery.desc: Threshold for being useable after Overheating and Heat Loss

Melee Damage.desc: Lower Bound and Upper Bound Damage. Effect shared with other weapons.

Beam Damage.desc: Damage per beam tick (the beam is 5 ticks)

Charging Time.desc: Charge-up time before the beam fires

More Shooting.desc: How many rounds each burst fires, and how fast they leave the barrel.
More Shooting.debug_desc: Shots Per Fire is the burst length, Rounds Per Second the cadence inside it. Raise the burst without raising the rate and the extra rounds all fire at the same instant. The gap BETWEEN bursts is Fire Recovery Time, on its own card.

Fire Recovery Time.debug_desc: The cooldown on trigger input after a shot, which on a burst weapon is the gap between bursts. The cadence inside a burst is Rounds Per Second, on the More Shooting card.

Projectiles Per Shot.desc: For every projectily, fire this many

Movement Penalty Type.debug_desc:
The `Movement Penalized` enum, which gates the Forward/Sideways Movement Penalty the Movement Penalties card tunes. Options are Always, When Zoomed, and When Zoomed Or Reloading; all four turrets ship at Always.

Offered only where BOTH halves already exist — a weapon with no Movement Penalties has nothing for the type to gate, and one with no Zoom card can never enter the zoomed state the other two options wait for. That is why it rides alongside those two cards rather than being offered on every weapon that happens to carry the field.

Set by NAME like every choice, though this enum happens to be ordered the same in Halo 3, ODST and Reach.

When Zoomed is deliberately NOT offered: turrets carry no ammunition and cannot be reloaded today, so it and When Zoomed Or Reloading would behave identically. Offering the broader one keeps the card correct if reloading is ever added to them.

Movement Penalties.desc: How much this turret slows you down while you are lugging it around.
Movement Penalties.debug_desc:
`Forward Movement Penalty` and `Sideways Movement Penalty` on the weapon, both moved together — they are one concept split into two fields, and setting them apart only makes strafing and advancing disagree. `Movement Penalized` gates when they apply and ships at `always` on all four turrets.

Only the four detached turrets set these at all: measured 0.40 in Halo 3 and 0.20 in ODST on Machine Gun, Plasma Cannon, Missile Pod and Flamethrower. The Flak Cannon looks like a turret but is a carried support weapon and sits at 0.00 everywhere, so it has no card. The card is written for Halo 3 and ODST picks it up through game inheritance, on the same tags.

1.0 would pin you in place; 0 removes the penalty entirely and lets you run with a turret at full speed. The '&' in the tag also covers each turret's INTEGRATED variant, the one bolted to a vehicle; those ship at 0.00 because you are seated, so an operator leaves them at 0 and only the carried version moves.

Per Round.desc: Heat per blob, fuel used per blob

Magnetism.desc: How hard your aim is pulled toward a target.
Magnetism.debug_desc:
`Magnetism Angle` and `Magnetism Range` are the pull on your reticle near a target, with `Magnetism Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) and Reach's `Magnetism Near Falloff Range` shaping where it fades. One decision, one input.

Autoaim.desc: How hard the game steers your shots onto a target.
Autoaim.debug_desc:
`Autoaim Angle` is the cone the game will bend a shot into, `Autoaim Range` how far out it does so, and `Autoaim Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) where that help starts tapering off. All three are one decision -- how much the game shoots for you -- so they share one input.

Autoaim is the shot bending toward the target; Magnetism is your reticle being pulled. They are separate fields and separate cards.

Shipped values differ wildly by weapon and game: the Halo 3 assault rifle is 5deg/15 with falloff 7.5, the sniper 1deg/10, and Reach's sniper 0.8deg/20. Cutting these to 0 removes aim assist entirely, which is the harder direction.

Rider Damage.desc: How much of this weapon's damage reaches someone sitting in a vehicle.
Rider Damage.debug_desc:
The three `Rider ... Damage Scale` fields on the weapon's damage tag, moved together because they are one question split by how the damage arrives: `Direct` when the shot hits the rider, `Maximum`/`Minimum Transfer` when it hits the vehicle and passes through.

The split is visible in the shipped values from Halo 3 on: bullet weapons run Direct 1 and explosives Direct 0 -- a rocket does not hit the rider, it transfers (the Halo 3 and ODST rocket carries Minimum Transfer 3). Halo 2 is the odd one out and sets Direct 1 on rockets and needler too, plus fractional 0.75 on both plasma weapons.

**Not offered in Reach.** The fields still exist there but do nothing -- tested in-game on Tip of the Spear, and Assembly documents them as deprecated in Reach. Halo 2 is confirmed working; Halo 3 and ODST use the same names at the same offsets (0x44/0x48/0x4C). Halo 1 has no rider fields at all.

Applied to every damage tag the weapon owns, not one hand-picked tag: the Needler also supercombines, the plasma pistol also fires an overcharged bolt, and the flak round has an impact as well as an explosion. Feedback tags -- trigger kick, overheat, misfire, detach -- are left out, since nothing rides them.

Raising these makes the weapon better at killing drivers and gunners, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Ramp Up.desc: How long the weapon takes to spin up to full rate, and to wind back down.
Ramp Up.debug_desc:
`Acceleration Time` is how long the weapon takes to reach its full rate of fire, `Deceleration Time` how long it takes to wind back down. Per barrel.

No card clamps Deceleration against Acceleration any more -- the constraint was removed on 2026-08-26 for retesting. The reasoning behind it was that guns spin up slowly and spin down fast, which holds for the plasma rifle, brute plasma rifle and needler, but is NOT universal: measuring every weapon that sets these fields disproves the stronger claim this text used to make: six weapon-games ship the OPPOSITE. Halo 3 and ODST's machinegun turret and plasma cannon both run 1.25 up / 2.0 down, Reach's plasma launcher 0.7 / 1.0, and Reach's spike rifle 0.0 / 0.2 -- it has no spin-up at all and still takes time to stop.

So the weapons that ship deceleration above acceleration deliberately carry NO constraint: clamping them would quietly rewrite their vanilla behaviour the first time the card was patched.

Also note Reach's stringid Rate Of Fire Acceleration/Deceleration fields are dead -- these numeric Time fields are the ones that carry the values.

Melee Seeking.desc: How generously your melee swing snaps onto a target.
Melee Seeking.debug_desc:
The melee damage pyramid: `Damage Pyramid Angles` y and p are the cone your swing sweeps (yaw and pitch), `Damage Pyramid Depth` how far in front of you it reaches.

Reach MOVED these into a `Melee Damage Parameters` block rather than deleting them, so the card carries a per-game block instead of needing a separate card. Halo 1 has none of these fields at all.

Reach also re-tuned them: Halo 2 through ODST ship a wide, flat 12.512 x 6.062 at depth 0.6, while Reach squares it off to 9.211 x 9.211 -- narrower horizontally, much taller. Outliers worth knowing: the Energy Blade at 24.046 x 13.817 depth 0.9, the ODST Gravity Hammer / Flamethrower / turrets at 11.459 x 11.459 depth 0.8, Reach's Gravity Hammer at 20.854 x 15.352 depth 1.0, and Reach's Needler, which alone kept the old 12.512 x 6.062.

Widening the angles or deepening it makes melee more forgiving, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Marked `ignore` on this weapon: the pyramid is what a MELEE weapon is built around, and every gun merely carries one because the engine gives every weapon a melee. The card stays wired and verified here, so enabling it is a one-word edit, but only the Energy Blade and Gravity Hammer offer it.

Movement Penalty Type.desc: When this turret slows you down: all the time, or only while you are zoomed in or reloading.
Movement Penalty Type.debug_desc:
The `Movement Penalized` enum, which gates the Forward/Sideways Movement Penalty the Movement Penalties card tunes. Options are Always, When Zoomed, and When Zoomed Or Reloading; all four turrets ship at Always.

Offered only where BOTH halves already exist — a weapon with no Movement Penalties has nothing for the type to gate, and one with no Zoom card can never enter the zoomed state the other two options wait for. That is why it rides alongside those two cards rather than being offered on every weapon that happens to carry the field.

Set by NAME like every choice, though this enum happens to be ordered the same in Halo 3, ODST and Reach.

When Zoomed is deliberately NOT offered: turrets carry no ammunition and cannot be reloaded today, so it and When Zoomed Or Reloading would behave identically. Offering the broader one keeps the card correct if reloading is ever added to them.

Movement Penalties.desc: How much this turret slows you down while you are lugging it around.
Movement Penalties.debug_desc:

Only the four detached turrets set these at all: measured 0.40 in Halo 3 and 0.20 in ODST on Machine Gun, Plasma Cannon, Missile Pod and Flamethrower. The Flak Cannon looks like a turret but is a carried support weapon and sits at 0.00 everywhere, so it has no card. The card is written for Halo 3 and ODST picks it up through game inheritance, on the same tags.

1.0 would pin you in place; 0 removes the penalty entirely and lets you run with a turret at full speed. The '&' in the tag also covers each turret's INTEGRATED variant, the one bolted to a vehicle; those ship at 0.00 because you are seated, so an operator leaves them at 0 and only the carried version moves.

Firing Noise.desc: How far away enemies hear you fire. Silent sneaks past them entirely; Shout pulls in the whole area.

Melee Seeking.desc: How generously your melee swing snaps onto a target.

Distribution Function.desc: Fans this weapon's shots out in a line instead of firing them all from one point.

Distribution Angle ships at 0 on every weapon in every game (81 of 81 read), hence zero_is 0.1 -- an operator works on 0.1 rather than multiplying 0 by something and still getting 0.

Zoom.desc: How far this weapon zooms — set Magnification Levels above 0 to give it a scope.

Reach was wired for this on 2026-08-27; its donors are the sniper rifle, DMR, needle rifle, magnum and rocket launcher -- the only five Reach weapons that ship any magnification.

Firing Noise.desc: How far away enemies hear you fire. Silent sneaks past them entirely; Shout pulls in the whole area.

Censused over 232 weapons in all five games, the names are not a ladder: Shout is the top tier (rockets, snipers, flak and AA cannons, Spartan Laser); Loud is the ordinary tier nearly everything ships with; Medium is the suppressed tier — ODST's automag and silenced SMG are the only two weapons anywhere that use it, plus Halo 1's sniper rifle; Silent is horns and cameras. Applied by NAME because the codes moved: Halo 1 through ODST store Silent, Medium, Loud, Shout, Quiet; Reach stores Silent, Quiet, Medium, Shout, Loud. Halo 1 keeps the field per Trigger, every later game per Barrel. Reach also simply hears further — 100 to 200 world units against 40 to 50 in the older games.
