`Maximum Range` and the velocity pair are the shot's reach and speed. The four damage-range fields are one row: Air and Water Damage Range are the same question asked of two media, and splitting them only invites setting them inconsistently.

GRAVITY. A second row appears wherever the projectile sets `Air Gravity Scale`. That matters most for the weapons which set it and NO air damage range at all -- measured, exactly the arcing launchers: Brute Shot (Halo 2 and 3), and Reach's Concussion Rifle, Grenade Launcher and Plasma Launcher. Their shot is a lobbed grenade whose flight gravity governs rather than a range falloff, so a Damage Range row alone would have given them a card that does nothing. Some ordinary weapons set air gravity too (Halo 1's pistol and shotgun at 1.0, Reach's magnum at 0.005) and get the row as well. Lower gravity flattens the arc and throws further.

Beam Damage.desc: Damage per beam tick (the beam is 5 ticks)

Magnetism.desc: How hard your aim is pulled toward a target.
Magnetism.debug_desc:
`Magnetism Angle` and `Magnetism Range` are the pull on your reticle near a target, with `Magnetism Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) and Reach's `Magnetism Near Falloff Range` shaping where it fades. One decision, one input.

**Halo 2 declares this pair TWICE** (weap root 0x19C and 0x210) and the first is a different, mostly-zero field -- reading it makes Halo 2 look like it barely uses magnetism. The real pair is the second, next to Autoaim, so every Halo 2 row here is pinned to `nth: 1`. Every other game states nth 0 explicitly, because a gamed value falls back to the nearest EARLIER game and Halo 3 would otherwise inherit Halo 2's 1.

This is the weapon's own magnetism. The general Magnetism card is a different thing -- matg's Magnetism Friction and Adhesion, the controller-level aim friction that applies to everything.

Autoaim.desc: How hard the game steers your shots onto a target.
Autoaim.debug_desc:
`Autoaim Angle` is the cone the game will bend a shot into, `Autoaim Range` how far out it does so, and `Autoaim Falloff Range` (Halo 3 onward) where that help starts tapering off. All three are one decision -- how much the game shoots for you -- so they share one input.

Autoaim is the shot bending toward the target; Magnetism is your reticle being pulled. They are separate fields and separate cards.

Shipped values differ wildly by weapon and game: the Halo 3 assault rifle is 5deg/15 with falloff 7.5, the sniper 1deg/10, and Reach's sniper 0.8deg/20. Cutting these to 0 removes aim assist entirely, which is the harder direction.

Weapon Swap Speed.desc: How fast you bring this weapon up and put it away. *0.5 is twice as fast.
Weapon Swap Speed.debug_desc:
Scales the `ready` and `put_away` first-person ANIMATIONS -- which is what weapon swap speed actually is. No weapon field drives it: `Ready Time` is non-zero on three weapons in Halo 3 and one in Reach (which is why testing it in Halo 2 showed nothing), `Weapon Ready-For-Use Time` on three, and ODST's promisingly-named `Weapon Ready 1st Person Animation Playback Scale` on none at all.

Measured lengths, at 30fps: Halo 3's assault rifle readies in 20 frames (0.67s) and stows in 6 (0.20s); the battle rifle 19/4; the shotgun 23/7; Halo 2's SMG 20/10. A swap plays the outgoing weapon's put_away and the incoming weapon's ready, so scaling both halves is what makes the whole exchange faster.

Same machinery as Reload Time -- the animation graph selects actions by label name, so this is the same code matching `ready`/`put_away` instead of `reload`. Halo Reach has no jmad layout yet, so it is not offered there (its Reload Time cards do not cover Reach either).

Reload Time.desc: How long you spend reloading. *0.5 is twice as fast.
Reload Time.debug_desc: In the MCC every magazine-fed weapon reloads on its first-person animation — the tag-side reload timer is inert — so this scales the animation's length. Scales both Master Chief and Arbiter.

Latch Time.desc: How long a stuck grenade waits before it can be detonated.
Latch Time.debug_desc:
`Maximum Latch Time To Arm` on the grenade projectile, stock 0.3s. Only two projectiles in any game set it: the player's Grenade Launcher and the Falcon's mounted version -- it is the arming delay that makes the weapon's stick-then-detonate trick work. New in Reach; no earlier game has the field.

Its sibling `Maximum Latch Time To Detonate` is 0 on every projectile in the game and is not offered. Verified in-game by kronfarore.

Raising it means a longer wait before a stuck grenade will answer the trigger.

Melee Seeking.desc: How generously your melee swing snaps onto a target.
Melee Seeking.debug_desc:
The melee damage pyramid: `Damage Pyramid Angles` y and p are the cone your swing sweeps (yaw and pitch), `Damage Pyramid Depth` how far in front of you it reaches.

Reach MOVED these into a `Melee Damage Parameters` block rather than deleting them, so the card carries a per-game block instead of needing a separate card. Halo 1 has none of these fields at all.

Reach also re-tuned them: Halo 2 through ODST ship a wide, flat 12.512 x 6.062 at depth 0.6, while Reach squares it off to 9.211 x 9.211 -- narrower horizontally, much taller. Outliers worth knowing: the Energy Blade at 24.046 x 13.817 depth 0.9, the ODST Gravity Hammer / Flamethrower / turrets at 11.459 x 11.459 depth 0.8, Reach's Gravity Hammer at 20.854 x 15.352 depth 1.0, and Reach's Needler, which alone kept the old 12.512 x 6.062.

Widening the angles or deepening it makes melee more forgiving, so the harder direction is DOWN.

Marked `ignore` on this weapon: the pyramid is what a MELEE weapon is built around, and every gun merely carries one because the engine gives every weapon a melee. The card stays wired and verified here, so enabling it is a one-word edit, but only the Energy Blade and Gravity Hammer offer it.

Accuracy Penalties.desc: How badly your aim is thrown off after reloading or switching to this weapon.
Accuracy Penalties.debug_desc:
`Reload Penalty` and `Switch Penalty`, per barrel -- the accuracy hit applied after a reload and after bringing the weapon up. New in Reach; no earlier game has either field.

Measured on every weapon in all five games. Only seven Reach weapons carry values: assault rifle 2.5/1.0, DMR 2.4/1.0, needle rifle 2.35/0.8, magnum 2.35/1.0, plasma rifle 4.0/2.0, sniper rifle 2.5/0.89, spike rifle 2.5/1.0. The plasma rifle is the outlier at nearly double everything else on both.

Reach's other two accuracy penalties, `Zoom Penalty` and `Jump Penalty`, are 0 on every weapon and are not offered. The Forward/Sideways Movement penalties are a different mechanic entirely and live on the Movement Penalties card.

The card is offered only on the seven weapons that ship a value, because an operator on a stored 0 does nothing -- the rest of Reach's weapons have no penalty to scale.

This weapon ships BOTH penalties at 0, so it is marked `ignore` and stays out of the offer pool: an operator on a stored 0 does nothing, and a card that reads as broken is worse than no card. The wiring is here and verified, so enabling it later -- for a run that wants to IMPOSE a penalty with `=` -- is a one-word edit.

Distribution Function.desc: Fans this weapon's shots out in a line instead of firing them all from one point.
Distribution Function.debug_desc:
Sets `Distribution Function` to `horizontal fan` and gives you `Distribution Angle` to tune. Both live per barrel (per trigger in Halo 1).

The angle is the whole effect: the function alone changes nothing you can see, so the set rides along with the angle row and only applies when you actually enter a value. Distribution Angle ships at 0 on every weapon in every game (81 of 81 read), hence zero_is 0.1 -- an operator works on 0.1 rather than multiplying 0 by something and still getting 0.

Despite the name the fan is NOT reliably horizontal -- tested in-game on the assault rifle, the line it spreads the shots along varies. What it does consistently is spread them along a line rather than from a point.

Only offered where the weapon already has a Projectiles Per Shot card: fanning a single projectile fans nothing, so the two belong together. `point` and `horizontal fan` are the only options every game shares; Reach adds `custom vectors` and `custom positions`, which need companion data to mean anything and are not offered.

Zoom.desc: How far this weapon zooms — set Magnification Levels above 0 to give it a scope.
Zoom.debug_desc:
`Magnification Levels` is how many zoom steps the weapon has and `Magnification Range` how far each goes. A weapon that ships with 0 levels has no zoom at all, which is exactly why it needs the card: an operator cannot multiply 0 into anything, so SET it (=1 or =2) to give the weapon a scope it never had.

Every game also adds a scope OVERLAY automatically when a scopeless weapon gains magnification, copying the widgets from a scoped donor on the same map (the 'Add a scope overlay to scopeless weapons' option, with a donor picker). Reach was wired for this on 2026-08-27; its donors are the sniper rifle, DMR, needle rifle, magnum and rocket launcher -- the only five Reach weapons that ship any magnification.

Firing Noise.desc: How far away enemies hear you fire. Silent sneaks past them entirely; Shout pulls in the whole area.
Firing Noise.debug_desc:
The `Firing Noise` enum: a noise event raised for AI hearing, whose reach is bounded by the listener's own `Hearing Distance` (char; actr in Halo 1). The same enum drives biped/vehicle Constant Sound Volume and projectile Impact/Detonation Noise — one shared AI sense of hearing.

This card sets the weapon AND its projectile's Impact and Detonation Noise to the same level, because the two are heard in different places: the firing noise goes off at you, the impact noise goes off wherever the round lands. Silencing only the weapon still announced every shot at the far end.

Censused over 232 weapons in all five games, the names are not a ladder: Shout is the top tier (rockets, snipers, flak and AA cannons, Spartan Laser); Loud is the ordinary tier nearly everything ships with; Medium is the suppressed tier — ODST's automag and silenced SMG are the only two weapons anywhere that use it, plus Halo 1's sniper rifle; Silent is horns and cameras. Quiet is used by no shipped weapon in any game.

Applied by NAME because the codes moved: Halo 1 through ODST store Silent, Medium, Loud, Shout, Quiet; Reach stores Silent, Quiet, Medium, Shout, Loud. Halo 1 keeps the field per Trigger, every later game per Barrel. Reach also simply hears further — 100 to 200 world units against 40 to 50 in the older games.

Magazine.desc: Changes to Munition for your weapon

More Shooting.desc: Turns one shot per pull into a burst. Raise Shots Per Fire for more rounds, Rounds Per Second to space them out.
More Shooting.debug_desc: This weapon sends one round per trigger pull, so Rounds Per Second does nothing until Shots Per Fire is above 1 — it is what spaces the rounds inside a single pull. How fast you can pull the trigger is Fire Recovery Time, on its own card.

Fire Recovery Time.desc: How fast you can pull the trigger again. Lower is faster.
Fire Recovery Time.debug_desc: The cooldown on trigger input after a shot. On a one-round-per-pull weapon this IS its rate of fire, so lowering it is the way to speed the weapon up.

Projectiles Per Shot.desc: For every projectily, fire this many

Explosion Damage.desc: How hard a supercombine explosion hits.
Explosion Damage.debug_desc:
Both super-detonation damage tags: the ATTACHED one, when the needles combine in a body, and the free-floating one when they combine in the air. The Needler models it the same way.

Separate from Needle Damage, which is the impact of a single needle -- a supercombine is its own event with its own damage and its own radius.

Explosion Radius.desc: How big the supercombine explosion is.
Explosion Radius.debug_desc: `Radius` and `Radius Max` on the free-floating super detonation, matching the Needler's Explosion Radius card.

Needle Timer.desc: How long needles stick before they combine and go off.
Needle Timer.debug_desc:
`Timer` / `Timer Max` on the needle projectile.

`Super Detonation Projectile Count` is how many needles must stick before they combine: 3 on the needle rifle, 6 on Reach's needler.

Ramp Up.desc: How long the weapon takes to spin up to full rate, and to wind back down.
Ramp Up.debug_desc:
`Acceleration Time` is how long the weapon takes to reach its full rate of fire, `Deceleration Time` how long it takes to wind back down. Per barrel.

No card clamps Deceleration against Acceleration any more -- the constraint was removed on 2026-08-26 for retesting. The reasoning behind it was that guns spin up slowly and spin down fast, which holds for the plasma rifle, brute plasma rifle and needler, but is NOT universal: measuring every weapon that sets these fields disproves the stronger claim this text used to make: six weapon-games ship the OPPOSITE. Halo 3 and ODST's machinegun turret and plasma cannon both run 1.25 up / 2.0 down, Reach's plasma launcher 0.7 / 1.0, and Reach's spike rifle 0.0 / 0.2 -- it has no spin-up at all and still takes time to stop.

So the weapons that ship deceleration above acceleration deliberately carry NO constraint: clamping them would quietly rewrite their vanilla behaviour the first time the card was patched.

Also note Reach's stringid Rate Of Fire Acceleration/Deceleration fields are dead -- these numeric Time fields are the ones that carry the values.

Sprint Speed.desc: How much faster sprinting actually moves you.

**Reach's Player Information block has TWO elements**, where Halo 3 and ODST have one: index 0 (Run Forward 2.2, multiplier 1.623) and index 1 (2.6, multiplier 1.4). Three Player Representations point into them -- two at index 0, one at index 1 -- i.e. the Spartan and the Elite. This card writes `index: "all"` so both move together rather than leaving one representation on stock values. Note the older Run Speed and Sneak Speed cards do NOT do this: they take the default index 0, so in Reach they only touch the first.

The sprint ability's own eqip tag holds no speed field at all -- only the energy meter -- which is why this card lives on matg while the rest of Sprint's cards sit on the ability.

Energy Drain.desc: How fast sprinting burns the ability meter.
Energy Drain.debug_desc:

Drain and cost are stored NEGATIVE, so a multiply makes them harsher, not gentler: -0.25 * 2 is -0.5, i.e. twice the drain. That is why the harder direction on those rows is DOWN.

Shipped rates differ per ability -- Sprint refills at 5.0 with a 4s pause, Armor Lock at 0.09 with 3s, the Drop Shield at 0.054 with 2s -- so the same multiplier is a different real change on each.

Shipped rates differ per ability -- Sprint refills at 5.0 with a 4s pause, Armor Lock at 0.09 with 3s, the Drop Shield at 0.054 with 2s -- so the same multiplier is a different real change on each.

Melee Delay.desc: How long enemies wait before swinging at you again.
Melee Delay.debug_desc:
`Melee Delay Base` and `Melee Delay Scale`, both per difficulty in matg's Difficulty block (0x140 and 0x150), present in all five games at the same offsets. Grouped because they are one number split in two: Base is the flat delay and Scale the per-difficulty multiplier on it.

The shipped values show which half carries the difficulty curve. From Halo 2 on, Base is 1.0 on every difficulty and Scale does all the work: Halo 2 runs 3.0/1.0/0.4/0.1 and Halo 3, ODST and Reach all run 4.0/2.0/1.0/0.25 (Easy/Normal/Heroic/Legendary). Halo 1 is the odd one: Scale 2.0/1.0/0.8/0.5, and Base is set only on Easy (1.5), leaving 0 on the other three.

That Halo 1 zero means the Base half of this card does nothing there on Normal, Heroic or Legendary — a multiply against 0 stays 0. It is left as a genuine zero rather than given a `zero_is`, because Halo 1 is the only game that leaves it unset and there is no sibling value to borrow. The Scale half still works in Halo 1, so the card is not dead there.

This is the non-berserk delay: a berserking Brute is governed by its own character tag, not by this.

Vision.desc: General enemy vision — distance, angles, peripheral — via the shared generic AI base. Exception: the Flood Combat forms.

Hearing Distance.desc: General enemy hearing range via the shared generic AI base. Exception: the Flood Combat forms.

Perception.desc: General enemy perception — notice chances and perception times via the shared generic AI base. Exception: the Flood Combat forms.

desc_overrides.Halo 3: General enemy perception — notice chances and perception times via the shared generic AI base. Halo 3 merged three fields into one. Exception: the Flood Combat forms.

Retreat.desc: General cower time and flee chance when a leader or peers die via the shared generic AI base. Exceptions: Grunts and Jackals.

Placement Properties.desc: General chance of spawning as an upgraded variant. Exceptions: most Elite and Grunt variants.

Grenade Properties.desc: General grenade behaviour — velocity, range, collateral. Exceptions: Grunts, Marines, SpecOps Elites and the Flood Combat forms.
Grenade Properties.debug_desc: The exception list is per game, and Brutes are only on it in Halo 2. From Halo 3 on their own Grenades block is empty on every brute char tag, so they inherit this one and this card is the ONLY way to tune their grenades. Measured on ODST: 9 of 72 char tags populate Grenades Properties — `ai\generic`, `elite_specops`, `grunt`, `grunt_ultra` and the four flood forms.

desc_overrides.Halo 2: General grenade behaviour — velocity, range, collateral. Exceptions: Brutes, Grunts, Marines, SpecOps Elites and the Flood Combat forms.

Firing Patterns.desc: General enemy rate of fire via the shared generic AI base. Exceptions: the Flood combat forms, Hunters and turrets, which define their own.

Accuracy.desc: How often enemy shots hit you, across the whole campaign.
Accuracy.debug_desc: Goes through the shared generic AI base. Grunts, Jackals, Hunters and the Flood forms define their own accuracy and are unaffected.

Maximum Firing Distance.desc: General enemy engagement range via the shared generic AI base. Exceptions: Grunts, Jackals and the Flood forms, which define their own.

AI Projectile Speed.desc: How fast AI-fired shots travel, and how hard the homing ones steer. Weapons with no tier set use the engine default and are unaffected.
AI Projectile Speed.debug_desc:
Two ladders on `proj *`, every projectile in the map, grouped into one row each because a difficulty tier is not a separate decision from its siblings.

VELOCITY. Halo 3 and ODST ship `AI Normal Velocity Scale` and `AI Legendary Velocity Scale`; Reach adds `AI Heroic Velocity Scale` and completes the ladder. The shipped values read as one: ghost bolt 0.75 / 0.90 / 1.10, plasma turret 0.66 / 0.80 / 1.00, revenant turret 0.40 / 0.50 / 0.60. 38 projectiles set at least one in Reach, 20 in ODST.

GUIDED. `AI Normal / Legendary Guided Angular Velocity Scale` are new in Reach -- no earlier game scales homing by difficulty. Only four projectiles use them: needler shard 0.15, rocket 0.1, plasma launcher 0.0001, falcon grenade 0.75. They scale the same Guided Angular Velocity the player's Homing card tunes, but only when an AI fires it.

Halo 2 has none of these fields and Halo 1 has no equivalent, so the card is Halo 3 onward. Raising either makes enemies harder: faster shots are harder to dodge and harder homing is harder to break.

targets.field: AI Normal Guided Angular Velocity Scale
AI Legendary Guided Angular Velocity Scale

Recharge Delay.desc: How long you have to keep hitting an Elite before its shields stop coming back.
Recharge Delay.debug_desc: `Stun Time` on the collision tag. Stock 12s, 8s for the Spec-Ops Elite. Halo 1 only — from Halo 2 on, the character tag's Shield Recharge Delay governs the AI instead and this field stops being the handle. The wildcard covers both Elite variants.

Leap.desc: How readily Elites vault obstacles to get at you.
Leap.debug_desc: Height and proximity. Stock 0.8 height / 0.4 proximity; the jetpack Elite is 2.0/0.5. Both fields are new in Reach — no earlier game has them.

Armor Lock.desc: How often Elites armour-lock to shrug off your shots, and how long it holds.
Armor Lock.debug_desc: Stock 15% chance and 5s cooldown on the base Elite; 30%/3.5s/0.5s/3s on the Ultra. The base Elite ships Safety and Maximum Duration at 0, so those two only bite on the Ultra until values are inserted. Raising chance and duration makes them harder; raising the cooldown makes them easier.

Halo 2 defines it on 9 of the 13 levels that field them and ODST on 8 of 8. Halo 3 has it on ONE, Floodgate (050) of 8 -- worth carding, but expect it to do nothing on the others.

From Halo 2 on every Elite variant ships ZERO entries in char > Grenades Properties and inherits them from `ai\generic` instead — measured on 05a and 010 — so a card aimed at the Elite’s own tag writes nothing that can take effect. The Halo 2 tag and targets were removed rather than left as dead references.

Betrayal.debug_desc:
Sets each human squad's Team to a hostile third faction, so they fight you AND the Covenant rather than simply swapping sides. A squad counts as human when every character it names matches a human tag and none is a loyal one.

ODST was wired 2026-08-31. Its squads hold characters in three sub-blocks instead of at a fixed offset, which is why it needs its own walk. Measured: ONI Alpha Site flips 18 squads, Data Hive 11, Coastal Highway 5, and Mombasa Streets 0 — the hub fields no human squads at all.

**On Data Hive and Coastal Highway this flips Buck and Dare**, who are also the escorts those levels can fail without. That is the skull working as intended, but expect it to make those two missions much harder or unfinishable.

Reach is NOT supported: its plugin describes the same shape one step along, but the block at `scnr+0x398` reads a count of zero on the shipped maps, so the real layout has to be located first.
